questions.prompt: What distinguishes a security incident from a security event?

options.text: An incident actually or imminently jeopardizes confidentiality, integrity, or availability
An incident is any observable occurrence, however trivial
An event always involves a nation-state

questions.explanation: Any observable occurrence is an event; it becomes an incident when it actually or imminently harms the CIA of systems or data.

questions.prompt: Order the NIST incident-response lifecycle phases.
questions.explanation: The lifecycle runs Preparation, Detection & Analysis, Containment/Eradication/Recovery, then Post-Incident Activity, looping back to improve preparation.

questions.prompt: The rule to collect the most ephemeral evidence (like RAM) first is called the order of ____.
questions.explanation: The order of volatility says to capture the most short-lived data first (registers, RAM) before disk, because powering off destroys memory evidence.

questions.prompt: Match each forensic concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: Documented record of who handled evidence, when, and how
Collect the most ephemeral evidence first
A verified copy you investigate instead of the live system

questions.explanation: Chain of custody keeps evidence admissible, order of volatility guides collection, forensic images preserve the original, and containment limits spread.

questions.prompt: Which are sound incident-response practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Isolate a compromised host from the network while preserving RAM evidence
Rebuild from known-good images rather than 'cleaning' a compromised host
Recover from tested, clean backups and monitor for re-entry
Improvise the plan during the incident

questions.explanation: Isolate-but-preserve, rebuild from known-good, and recover from clean backups are best practices; improvising instead of preparing is the classic failure.

questions.prompt: Why is 'clean the infected machine' usually not sufficient for eradication?

options.text: A compromised host may hide persistence you can't be sure you removed, so rebuild from known-good
It takes longer than paying a ransom

questions.explanation: You can't prove a compromised host is fully clean (e.g. a hidden rootkit), so the safe practice is rebuilding from a trusted image and restoring clean data.
